original_snapshot: Small asset on a tall transparent canvas. A simple rectangular blue ledge dominates; its front has a deep navy lower portion and broad, mostly flat top shading.

Three separated, narrow closed coral posts: teal at the upper center, purple toward both lower sides. Their tips and stems are visibly faceted; the snapshot contains little layered rock or clustered coral structure.
The snapshot is a registration reference for the actual starting export. Its outline alone does not establish a connection profile or allowable native changes.
fixed_imagegen_target: Blue stone becomes an organized terrace of chunky, softly rounded, irregular rock blocks, with a strong cyan top-plane highlight and deeper blue side planes.
A tall teal multi-tube coral cluster supplies the main vertical accent; two lower magenta-purple clusters flank it. Open, dark recessed mouths with thick pale rims give the tubes readable thickness.

Tube sides retain broad stylized facets and taper/lean rather than resembling uniform straight cylinders. Small raised nodules, rounded teal stones and perforated dark blue sponge-like pebbles add purposeful secondary detail.

Broad warm mint/yellow highlights, luminous cyan transitions, magenta rims and soft contact shading express a polished cartoon material. Large masses and a clear color hierarchy carry the image before tiny decoration.

The target expands form, construction, decoration and apparent part count substantially beyond the original. This is aesthetic direction; its taller fuller silhouette and staged terrace cannot be treated as proof of native registration or connector compatibility.
warm_soft_reference: The green leaf planter uses large legible color planes, rounded/chamfered edge transitions, a broad warm upper-left light, bright yellow-green highlight edges and soft dark contact recesses.
Smooth cartoon softness coexists with visible faceted planar structure. The orange planter has thick rounded rim and base volume rather than a flat painted outline.
For reef-end this supports rounded solid geometry, clear plane lighting, restrained soft shadow and readable saturated color families; it does not require adding planter-specific shapes.
own_visual_interpretation.family_concept: The supplied family-concept presents the same coral-and-blue-rock language at a smaller size on a tall transparent canvas. It was inspected before the actual warm-soft reference was located, and remains a separate input role.

actual_original_native_findings.construction: One 32-vertex/26-polygon continuous faceted core, three 14-vertex/9-polygon stems, three 12-vertex/20-triangle closed tips, one 12-vertex/20-triangle polyp, and one empty root.
actual_original_native_findings.materials: Original own materials include dark/light blue rock, purple, teal and coral; no external image textures are used by these source materials.
actual_original_native_findings.geometry_observation: Core uses four repeated 8-vertex cross-sections at x=-0.5, -0.2, 0.14, 0.34. It is a continuous shaped prism with closed end caps. This describes source topology only and does not freeze the construction method.
actual_original_native_findings.measurement_method: Raw original mesh vertices transformed by recursively composed parent world, matrix_parent_inverse and matrix_basis. All collection objects have no constraints and all meshes have no modifiers, asserted by driver. The saved unlinked collection matrix_world values are stale identity and are recorded but not used for bounds.
actual_original_native_findings.measurement_caveat: The native library collection is unlinked/hidden from its active evaluation context, and saved matrix_world was identity even for translated/scaled coral. Rejected direct-depsgraph bounds are retained in unlinked-stale-measurements-rejected.json solely as a diagnostic. Only final authored-transform measurements are usable.
